findings.evidence: grep -c on the four lemma names across TauCeti: 14 occurrences, all in Basic.lean — the "104 uses would be at risk" argument does not apply, since those 104 uses reference `locSubring` and lemma statements that stay identical. `grep -n expose Basic.lean` returns only prose, no `@[expose]`.
findings.fix: Define `locSubring P T s S := locBaseSubring P.ringOfDefinition T s S` and prove the four `locSubring` lemmas from their `locBaseSubring` counterparts. Their statements are unchanged, so no use site moves. Keep `locSubring_eq_locBaseSubring` as the public (`rfl`) identification, since bodies stay unexposed.
findings.issue: `locSubring` keeps a verbatim copy of `locBaseSubring`'s body (`Subring.closure ((algebraMap A S) '' … ∪ Set.range …)`, lines 81 vs 137) and a verbatim copy of its interface: `locSubring_def` (158) vs `locBaseSubring_def` (87), `divBy_mem_locSubring` (172) vs `divBy_mem_locBaseSubring` (101), `algebraMap_mem_locSubring` (179) vs `algebraMap_mem_locBaseSubring` (94), `locSubring_le_iff` (188) vs `locBaseSubring_le_iff` (109). Two definitions and two lemma sets for one object is duplicated public API; and since the file is `public section` with no `@[expose]`, the bodies are opaque downstream, so consumers cannot move between the two forms by defeq — the PR's claim that the `rfl` bridge "costs nothing at any future use site" does not hold outside this file.

findings.evidence: Lines 111-113 vs 191-193 of Basic.lean; the `mono_base` proof at 120-128 already has to destructure the image (`obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := hx`) because of the image form.
findings.fix: State `locBaseSubring_le_iff` as `locBaseSubring B T s S ≤ C ↔ (∀ a ∈ B, algebraMap A S a ∈ C) ∧ ∀ t ∈ T, divBy t s ∈ C`, then `locSubring_le_iff := locBaseSubring_le_iff ..`.
findings.issue: `locBaseSubring_le_iff` states the base condition as an image inclusion `(algebraMap A S) '' (B : Set A) ⊆ (C : Set S)`, while the parallel `locSubring_le_iff` (line 188) uses the pointwise `∀ a ∈ P.ringOfDefinition, algebraMap A S a ∈ R`. The two universal properties of the same object have different shapes, so a consumer must convert by hand and `locSubring_le_iff` cannot be obtained as a specialization.

findings.evidence: Declaration list from Basic.lean: locBaseSubring has only `_def`, `algebraMap_mem_`, `divBy_mem_`, `_le_iff`, `_mono_base` (lines 79-128), while locSubring additionally has `_empty`/`_mono`/`_insert` (203-235).
findings.fix: State `locBaseSubring_empty` (`@[simp]`), `locBaseSubring_mono` (in `T`) and `locBaseSubring_insert` (`@[simp]`) at the general level and derive the three `locSubring` forms from them, keeping their existing `@[simp]` annotations.
findings.issue: The `T`-side API developed for `locSubring` — `locSubring_empty` (`@[simp]`, 203), `locSubring_mono` (212), `locSubring_insert` (`@[simp]`, 222, the Finset recursion) — has no `locBaseSubring` counterpart. `simp` matches syntactically and bodies are unexposed, so none of these fire on `locBaseSubring Aplus T s S`; the Layer 3.1 consumer this PR exists to serve gets only intro lemmas and `le_iff`, with no normal form for `∅` or `insert` and no monotonicity in `T`.

summary: The PR names the general construction but leaves `locSubring` as a verbatim duplicate definition with a duplicate four-lemma interface, so the post-PR surface carries two parallel APIs for one object. The general form is also missing the `∅`/`insert`/`mono` lemmas the file already develops for the specialization, and its universal property is stated in a different shape than the specialized one.
